title: performance(canary): adaptive-thresholds-and-hysteresis-for-rollout-guards
author: Evelyn Park
description:
Motivation: Our existing performance canary rollout guard used fixed absolute thresholds which led to noisy halts on low-throughput routes and missed regressions on high-throughput routes. This PR implements adaptive thresholds and hysteresis to reduce false positives and make auto-detection resilient across a wider variety of traffic profiles.

What I changed: 1) Added adaptive threshold computation that combines baseline percentile modelling (P95/P99) with configurable relative tolerance. The guard now computes route-specific baselines from the last N successful canary runs and derives both an absolute and a relative threshold. 2) Introduced hysteresis windows (configurable in minutes/requests) so a transient spike does not immediately fail a canary; the guard requires sustained breach before halting. 3) Integrated a two-stage signal: short-window latency spikes trigger increased sampling and KV-cache warmup; only sustained degradation triggers a halt. 4) Exposed config knobs in the canary policy API and Console UI (docs updated). 5) Added a synthetic perf-canary CI job that runs simplified canaries on a small cluster to catch obvious regressions on PRs touching runtime/scheduler and batching code.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for threshold calculator and hysteresis logic - [x] Integration tests with perf-canary harness - [x] Console config UI + docs - [x] Load-tested locally with mixed route profiles - [x] Added rollout notes and feature flag (rollout guarded behind `adaptive_canary_thresholds`)

Backward compatibility: This is behind a feature flag and defaults to the old fixed-threshold behavior. Customers using custom canary policies will need to review their policies if they opt-in to adaptive thresholds.

Notes: There is a follow-up planned to persist baseline windows to Redis to survive control-plane restarts (ENG-11002).

review_comments: Miguel Santos (reviewer): Overall looks good. Two concerns: 1) baseline window size default might be too small for low-traffic routes, 2) you're computing P99 from a sliding window in memory — what happens on control plane restart? Can we persist state?
Author (Evelyn): Thanks — added config for baseline_window_size and set default to 72h (configurable). Persisting baseline is tracked in ENG-11002, noted in the PR description.
Priya Desai (reviewer): Hysteresis logic needs clear unit tests showing time-based behavior. Also add a comment explaining why we use combined absolute+relative thresholds rather than pure relative.

Author: Added hysteresis unit tests that simulate sustained breach over the configured window and updated comments in adaptive.go explaining rationale (low-qps routes need absolute floors to avoid noise).
Noah Thompson (sre): CI perf job failure on first run showed a false negative due to KV-cache cold start; recommend adding an initial warmup phase before measuring.
Author: Added KV-cache warmup step in perf-canary CI job and adjusted evaluator to allow an initial warmup period when sample_count < min_samples.

release_notes: Improved canary rollout guards: adaptive route-specific thresholds and hysteresis reduce false positives and enable more robust automated canaries. Feature is behind feature flag adaptive_canary_thresholds.
notes: Follow-up: persist baseline windows to Redis (ENG-11002), consider adding percentile smoothing for very-low-qps routes.
